description:
Diner Kitsch is the Baby Boomer & Silent Generation revival of various 1950s-1960s cultural iconography, design, and kitsch associated with diner, drive-ins and malt shop culture.

It is characterized by the stylized re-use of mid-century American roadside dining imagery (neon signage, chrome accents, checkerboard floors, vinyl upholstery, jukeboxes, and other decorative elements) within later media, commercial spaces, and consumer goods that evoke a nostalgic, often idealized version of this era. culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): carefreeness, 50s/60s nostalgia

visualDNA.Overview: Furniture and textures incorporate high-gloss laminate tables, prominent polished chrome edging on stools, deep vinyl, channel-back tufted booths, and counter trims, featuring deep vinyl and leather booths in tones and pastel with channel-back tufting, incorporating elements such as the high-contrast white-and-black checkerboard floor tile patterns, polished chrome edges on bar stools, counter trims and tables, along with the color palette that incorporates mint greens, bold reds, turquoise paired with white and black and hot pinks.
